guardrail.statement: This decision only approves the RabbitMQ capacity, queue-type, resource, and security envelope for later backend bootstrap work.

followup_provisioning_status.statement: The current service baseline may show Docker Engine, Docker Compose, and RabbitMQ as deployed only after later protected backend bootstrap/apply work. AMQP, management, and Prometheus listeners remain loopback-only, and this #79 decision remains the capacity/security approval record rather than a provisioning change.

release_support.erlang_28_policy: Do not select Erlang/OTP 28 for an upgraded 4.3 cluster unless a later release note review approves it; RabbitMQ 4.3 docs mark Erlang 28 as only partially supported.

decision.single_node_ha_statement: The initial single RabbitMQ node provides durable local transport only; it is not broker high availability and it is not quorum replication.

retry_dlq_strategy.consumer_ack_rule: Commit stage state and confirm downstream retry, DLQ, or next-stage publish before acking the source delivery.
retry_dlq_strategy.confirm_failure_behavior: If retry, DLQ, or next-stage publish is nacked or times out, do not ack the source delivery; let RabbitMQ redeliver and rely on stage inbox/outbox idempotency.
quorum_dlx_caveats_for_future_review: quorum at-least-once dead lettering requires quorum queues and internal publisher confirms
dead-letter target availability and duplicate target routing must be monitored before source messages are acked
queue length overflow must use reject-publish or reject-publish-dlx, not drop-head
retaining source messages until internal confirm increases memory, disk, and CPU pressure
the stream feature flag and RabbitMQ release notes must be checked before enabling quorum at-least-once dead lettering

upgrade_path.initial_install: Install the pinned 4.3.3 linux/amd64 image only through a later reviewed backend PR and protected apply.
upgrade_path.patch_upgrade: Move from one 4.3.x patch to another by updating the pinned digest, running the RabbitMQ benchmark workflow, exporting definitions, confirming no resource alarms, and applying through protected backend check/apply.
upgrade_path.minor_upgrade: RabbitMQ 4.3.x can be upgraded only from 4.2.x. For any future 4.4+ path, review target release notes, version upgradability, Erlang compatibility, and stable feature flags before changing the digest.
upgrade_path.feature_flags: Before every upgrade, confirm all stable feature flags for the current release are enabled; after upgrade, enable newly stable feature flags only after health checks pass.

measured_host_headroom.kernel: Linux backend 7.0.0-28-generic #28-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun Jun 21 01:01:36 UTC 2026 x86_64

cpu.headroom_summary: Low observed load relative to 4 vCPU; reserve RabbitMQ for bounded worker transport and keep Qwen/local AI off this host unless a later issue measures it.

memory.headroom_summary: About 8.89 GiB available at capture. Initial RabbitMQ is capped to 1 GiB with a 512 MiB broker memory watermark.

disk.headroom_summary: About 70.02 GiB available at capture. Initial RabbitMQ disk alarm is 20 GiB free to protect PostgreSQL, backups, logs, and host recovery room.

io.headroom_summary: Observed disk pressure was low, but the disk is rotational. Queue caps keep broker backlog bounded and PostgreSQL remains the recovery source.

file_descriptors.headroom_summary: Use explicit container nofile limits; do not inherit the interactive shell limit.

docker.headroom_summary: Docker/Compose must be installed only by a later protected backend apply. This issue does not install Docker or RabbitMQ on the backend host.

postgresql.headroom_summary: PostgreSQL is active and lightweight at capture; broker limits preserve database, backup, and restore headroom.

qwen_or_local_ai.headroom_summary: No Qwen, Ollama, AI, or LLM service was observed. Approval-stage local AI deployment remains a later capacity decision.

backup.latest_timer_window_utc: backup around 03:17 UTC, verify around 04:17 UTC, restore drill weekly around 05:17 UTC
backup.headroom_summary: RabbitMQ disk cap and disk alarm leave room for backup activity; broker messages are not treated as backup-only recovery state.

firewall_and_listeners.headroom_summary: RabbitMQ AMQP, management, and Prometheus listeners must remain private-only and must not add public ports.

observed_service_headroom.headroom_summary: Existing services leave enough RAM for a 1 GiB-capped broker, but RabbitMQ must be paused or scaled down before expensive host maintenance if alarms fire.

retry.retention_policy: retry queues hold delayed work only until the next bounded attempt; exhausted messages move to the route DLQ through application-confirmed transfer

dlq.replay_policy: manual approved replay in bounded batches after sanitized failure metadata is reviewed

benchmark_evidence.production_host_reason: No broker was provisioned by this #79 design issue. At the #79 design-capture time, the backend host had no Docker Engine installed; later protected backend bootstrap issues may provision the approved loopback-only broker.

local_attempt.evidence: Local Docker CLI could not connect to a daemon. No local or production broker was started.

comparison.expected_single_node_behavior: Lower single-node overhead for the bounded transport role; durability depends on the single broker disk and publisher confirms.
comparison.ha_statement: No broker high availability on one node.

comparison.expected_single_node_behavior: Runs Raft/quorum machinery without tolerating node loss because the group size is one.
comparison.ha_statement: No broker high availability on one node.

benchmark_evidence.benchmark_acceptance: The CI benchmark must complete before any later RabbitMQ bootstrap PR is applied. A performance regression does not by itself choose quorum on one node; it opens a new capacity decision.

amqp.binding: private Docker network only; optional loopback host binding for protected maintenance must be reviewed separately

management.binding: 127.0.0.1 only or private maintenance network only
management.access_path: SSH tunnel or protected backend workflow; never proxied by Caddy to the public internet

network_security.tls_trust_boundary: Same-host worker services may use the private Docker network without public TLS. Any off-host AMQP, management, or scrape path requires TLS plus a private network or SSH tunnel before approval.

credentials.default_guest_user_policy: delete or disable for the worker vhost during bootstrap
credentials.service_identity_policy: least-privilege route-scoped publisher and consumer users; no worker service receives break-glass admin credentials
credentials.stage_runtime_identity_policy: Starting with #117, forwarding services that expose one RabbitMQ URL may use their route-scoped consumer secret as a stage_runtime identity that reads only its input queue and writes only the main/retry/DLQ exchanges needed for its declared outbound route.
credentials.monitoring_identity_policy: monitoring tag only, no configure/write/read permissions on queues

network_security.audit_logs: Ship RabbitMQ auth, connection, channel, alarm, topology, and operator-action logs through backend Alloy with low-cardinality labels and no message payload logging.

alert_thresholds.memory_alarm: critical when RabbitMQ memory alarm is active for 5 minutes
alert_thresholds.disk_alarm: critical when RabbitMQ disk alarm is active for 5 minutes or root free bytes approaches 20 GiB
alert_thresholds.queue_age: warning when any main queue age exceeds 15 minutes; critical at 30 minutes
alert_thresholds.dlq_growth: warning on any new DLQ message; critical when a route DLQ grows for two consecutive checks
alert_thresholds.publisher_confirms: warning on confirm timeout or nack rate above 1 percent over 10 minutes
alert_thresholds.consumer_lag: warning when messages_ready plus messages_unacked exceeds 50 percent of the route cap

monitoring_and_maintenance.maintenance: RabbitMQ topology, credential rotation, replay, purge, and service scaling must use reviewed protected backend changes or future fixed workflows behind production-backend approval.
monitoring_and_maintenance.definition_backup: Export broker definitions after topology changes for fast rebuild evidence. Do not treat broker queue contents as the only backup.

recovery_model.authoritative_recovery_source: backend PostgreSQL stage inbox, outbox, attempt, reconciliation, and watermark tables
recovery_model.broker_backup_role: topology and operator evidence only; broker messages alone are not the disaster-recovery source
recovery_model.rpo: Confirmed PostgreSQL stage/outbox state has zero intentional data loss. Unconfirmed broker deliveries are replayed or reconciled from PostgreSQL after broker loss.
recovery_model.rto: Target 30 minutes to rebuild a single-node broker topology after the host and Docker runtime are available, then replay pending outbox rows before resuming producers.
broker_loss_procedure: Recreate RabbitMQ vhost, exchanges, policies, queues, users, and permissions from backend source control.
Replay pending stage outbox rows with publisher confirms.
Run reconciliation watermarks and shadow parity checks before production-write resume.

managed_or_three_node_migration_trigger.decision: Stay single-node for initial shadow deployment; move to managed RabbitMQ or a reviewed three-node design when workload or recovery evidence exceeds the single-host envelope.
triggers: Any requirement for broker availability through loss of the backend VPS.
Sustained RabbitMQ memory use above 60 percent of its 1 GiB cap after concurrency tuning.
RabbitMQ disk or memory alarms recur more than twice in one week under normal workload.
Any main queue exceeds 50 percent of its cap or 15 minutes of age for two consecutive observation windows.
DLQ replay volume or recovery drills cannot meet the 30 minute broker rebuild target.
Worker throughput requires more than 24 app connections, 128 channels, or 128 in-flight confirms per channel.
Backlog or latency requires queue replication, live broker upgrade tolerance, or off-host maintenance.
